info.title: rulebearing: one architecture rule set for TypeScript, .NET and Python
info.description: Rulebearing as a dotnet tool: one architecture rule set for TypeScript, .NET and Python, deterministic guardrails an agent can check its own changes against. Carries the rulebearing binary for Linux x64 (glibc and musl) and arm64, macOS arm64 and x64, and Windows x64.

`$RULEBEARING_NODE`)

options.name: --mode
options.description:
How .NET is read: compiled (the default) from the built assemblies and PDBs, or source
from the .cs files without a build, every edge marked approximate; wins over
languages.dotnet.mode
- compiled: From the built assemblies and their portable PDBs: the gate
- source:   From the .cs files, without a build: namespace-level, every edge approximate,
never the gate

options.name: --progress
options.description:
Show progress on stderr
- cli-feedback:    Stage names on stderr as they start
- performance-log: Stage timings and memory on stderr
- ndjson:          One JSON object per stage on stderr
- none:            Nothing

options.name: --no-progress
options.description: Show no progress

options.name: --info
options.description: Show the languages, extensions and parsers this build supports

options.name: --init
options.description:
Write a first configuration instead of cruising, as `init` does, never asking: `yes` (the
default), or `x-scripts` to also add run scripts to package.json

options.name: --preset
options.description:
With --init: presets to use, as `init --preset` takes them: languages (typescript, dotnet,
python) instead of the ones found, and frameworks (nextjs, clean-architecture, django,
fastapi, vertical-slices), opinions that are off unless named
- typescript:         TypeScript and JavaScript: `rulebearing:typescript`
- dotnet:             .NET: `rulebearing:dotnet`
- python:             Python: `rulebearing:python`
- nextjs:             Next.js route and server boundaries: `rulebearing:nextjs`
- clean-architecture: Domain, Application, Infrastructure and Presentation:
`rulebearing:clean-architecture`
- django:             Django's models, views, URLs and migrations: `rulebearing:django`
- fastapi:            FastAPI's routers, services and repositories: `rulebearing:fastapi`
- vertical-slices:    Features independent of each other: `rulebearing:vertical-slices`

options.name: --no-liveness
options.description: Do not check whether rules match anything; the same as --liveness off

options.name: --liveness
options.description:
Rules that match nothing: strict fails the run (exit 2), warn reports them, off skips the
check. Default: strict for a rulebearing.* configuration, warn for a dependency-cruiser
one (ADR-0032)
- strict: Fails the run with exit 2 (the default for a native configuration)
- warn:   Reported in `summary.vacuousRules` and on stderr, without changing the exit code
(the default for a dependency-cruiser configuration, which dependency-cruiser does not
check)
- off:    Not checked

options.name: --strict-schema
options.description:
json: strip every Rulebearing addition so the output validates against cruise-result
18.2.0

options.name: --max-findings
options.description: agent: the most violations shown per rule

options.name: --color
options.description:
Colour terminal output
- auto:   When stdout is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is not set
- always: Always
- never:  Never
[default: auto]

options.name: --from-hook
options.description:
Answer as a Claude Code Stop hook: the agent report as the reason to keep going when there
are errors, exit 0 always

options.name: --affected
options.description:
Only report the modules changed since REVISION (default main), committed or not, and every
module that reaches them, as dependency-cruiser does; with a rulebearing.* configuration,
also every violation on their edges that leave them. .NET source files map to their types'
modules

options.name: --affected-depth
options.description:
With --affected or options.affected: how many steps of dependents to include; 0 (the
default) for all

options.name: --exit-code-mode
options.description:
How the error count becomes the exit code: default (the count) or strict (10 + the count,
so 2 and 3 are never a count)
- default: The error count, capped at 255, as dependency-cruiser exits
- strict:  10 plus the error count when there is one, capped at 255, so 2 and 3 only ever
mean an untrustworthy run and an invalid configuration
[default: default]

options.name: --allow-approximate-gate
options.description:
Let a run read in source mode (--mode source) decide the exit code, or be written with
--strict-schema, for a local script; without it such a run exits 2, since its edges are
approximate. Never in CI (ADR-0011)

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help (see a summary with '-h')
Exit codes:
0       no error-severity violation
1-255   the number of error-severity violations, capped at 255, from a reporter that gates:
err, err-long, null, teamcity, azure-devops, github-annotations, agent
(json, csv and text exit 0, as in dependency-cruiser)
2       the run cannot be trusted: zero modules, an unsupported file, a vacuous rule, or a
.NET graph read with --mode source deciding a gate (--allow-approximate-gate lets a
local script have the count)
3       the configuration is invalid
A run with exactly 2 or 3 error violations also exits 2 or 3; the report says which it was.
--exit-code-mode strict exits 10 + n for n error violations instead (capped at 255), so 2 and 3
only ever mean an untrustworthy run and an invalid configuration.

options.name: --help
options.description:
Print help (see a summary with '-h')
Exit codes:
0       no error-severity violation
1-255   the number of error-severity violations, capped at 255, from a reporter that gates:
err, err-long, null, teamcity, azure-devops, github-annotations, agent
(json, csv and text exit 0, as in dependency-cruiser)
2       the run cannot be trusted: zero modules, an unsupported file, a vacuous rule, or a
.NET graph read with --mode source deciding a gate (--allow-approximate-gate lets a
local script have the count)
3       the configuration is invalid
A run with exactly 2 or 3 error violations also exits 2 or 3; the report says which it was.
--exit-code-mode strict exits 10 + n for n error violations instead (capped at 255), so 2 and 3
only ever mean an untrustworthy run and an invalid configuration.
